reason:
Harrison 2009 (Nature) — foundational NIA-ITP rapamycin lifespan study.
The paper exists and is canonical; verified by the reviewer against
PubMed metadata. Auto-retrieval intermittently fails because NCBI's PMC
service returns a reCAPTCHA challenge under concurrent load and the
publisher Unpaywall URL (Nature) is paywalled-OA. This is a documented
retrieval-layer gap, NOT a license to manually include the paper —
the engine must fetch verified bytes for the universal contract to
pass.
evidence_quote: Here we report that rapamycin, an inhibitor of the mTOR pathway, extends median and maximal lifespan of both male and female mice when fed beginning at 600 days of age. On the basis of age at 90% mortality, rapamycin led to an increase of 14% for females and 9% for males.
action_required: wire stable OA mirror or supply verified Nature PDF; until then sentinel gate must surface this as WARN

Bitto 2016 transient-rapamycin study (eLife, OA). The auto-judge has
intermittently landed this as include conf 1.00 and sometimes as
unclear conf 0.50 depending on prompt variance. When the auto-judge
contract-passes Bitto with mouse/intervention/control/endpoint quotes
extracted from the parsed bytes, it joins the primary corpus normally.
This manual asserts paper availability for sentinel-recall accounting
only; it does NOT promote the paper into the corpus.
evidence_quote: A brief 3-month treatment of middle-aged mice with the mTOR inhibitor rapamycin produced an immediate, persistent improvement in healthspan and increased survival, with adult-onset transient rapamycin treatment significantly extending median and maximum lifespan in male mice.
action_required: judge prompt stabilisation so this paper passes the universal contract reliably

reason:
Off-topic for primary lifespan corpus. Paper studies metformin-driven
nephrotoxicity in acute kidney injury (AKI); rapamycin appears only as
one of several comparator drugs tested for protective effect against
I/R-induced renal damage. The "100% survival" quoted refers to AKI
survival over days, not lifespan extension.
evidence_quote: we treated mice with AKI induced by renal ischemia-reperfusion (I/R) with different drugs alone. Notably, nicotinamide, resveratrol, rapamycin, and senolytics, but not metformin, showed some to no protective effects on AKI based on various readouts of renal health and function

reason:
Side-effect / mechanism study, not a primary lifespan-extension trial.
The paper uses rapamycin at "lifespan-extending doses" to ask whether
muscle mitochondrial content / endurance are compromised. Lifespan is
referenced as a known prior result, not measured here.
evidence_quote: Therefore, we tested whether rapamycin, at the same doses used to extend lifespan, affects mitochondrial function in skeletal muscle.

reason:
SRN-901 (a novel compound) is the primary intervention; rapamycin is a
positive-control comparator. Per pre-specified PICO ("primary
intervention = rapamycin/sirolimus"), this is comparator usage, not a
primary rapamycin trial.
evidence_quote: While rapamycin increased lifespan in adult mice, nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN), and nicotinamide riboside (NR) did not show significant differences in median lifespan compared to placebo.
